sites.name: TYSON VALLEY POWDER FARM

facts.summary: EPA Region 7's 2018 release says the Tyson Valley Powder Farm won a national Federal Facility Excellence in Site Reuse award in the non-NPL category. It describes reuse already in place: the Washington University Tyson Research Center's Endangered Wolf Center, Lone Elk Park and a World Bird Sanctuary. This recognizes existing reuse, not a new project.
facts.reference: Tyson Valley Powder Farm in Eureka, Mo., Wins National Federal Facility Excellence in Site Reuse Award
facts.quote: Now, the site hosts the Washington University Tyson Research Center's Endangered Wolf Center

gaps: Searched the site name, Eureka, and Lone Elk Park with 2025 and 2026 terms. No news, county, or developer item on a current project, sale, or cleanup at the Powder Farm was found.
The Powder Farm is also called Lone Elk Park and West Tyson County Park. The park items found are undated (a radio segment and a bison-calf item with no year), so none are cited.
The 2018 EPA award is the most recent dated item found, and it names no county. St. Louis County parks releases and Army Corps FUDS records were not checked.

sites.name: SANGAMON ORDNANCE PLANT

facts.summary: Illinois EPA fact sheet 4 (May 2005) on the Formosa Plastics site west of Illiopolis, the former Borden PVC plant within the ordnance plant land. The state did not yet know the extent of the chemicals left on site, and it said the remedial investigation would not fully start until demolition was complete. The sheet is about 20 years old, and no later agency status was found.
facts.reference: Formosa Plastics site, Illiopolis: Illinois EPA fact sheet 4
facts.quote: The Illinois EPA does not yet know the extent of chemicals that remain.

gaps: Searched the site name, Illiopolis, the water tower, and Formosa Plastics cleanup for 2024 to 2026. No redevelopment, developer, incentive, or cleanup news for the ordnance plant land was found. The 2024 to 2025 Formosa hits concern a St. James Parish, Louisiana project and are excluded.

A 2024 News-Gazette column (Tom Kacich) reports that most of the land has returned to farming and that the Illiopolis water tower was designated a county landmark. Opening it returned HTTP 429, so nothing from it is cited. Verify before use.
An Illinois Times item on a proposed landmark for the water tower is undated in the results and was not opened, so it is not cited.
The only agency cleanup record opened is the May 2005 fact sheet. Groundwater, soil, and dioxin remedy status after 2005 is not verified.

sites.name: RICHMOND NAS

facts.summary: Miami Today reported in July 2000 that Portico Group was selected to create a new master plan for Metrozoo and the former Richmond Naval Air Station in South Dade. The plan was to be covered by $12 million in 1996 Safe Neighborhood Park bond funds, with a final document expected in April 2001. The article covers planning only, not reuse of the base, and no outcome was found.
facts.reference: Firm Named To Redesign Plan For Zoo Richmond Base
facts.quote: to create a new master plan for Metrozoo and the former Richmond Naval Air Station in South Dade.

gaps: Searched the site name, Richmond Heights, Chapman Field, and Zoo Miami or Metrozoo planning for 2024 and 2025. No current development project, developer, incentive, or cleanup news for the former air station land was found.
Most 'Richmond' results were other places (Richmond VA Navy Hill, Richmond Heights MO, Richmond Heights OH) and are excluded.

A search result mentions an April 2024 approval for a historical marker at the Miami-Dade Military Museum, in the former station headquarters building. It was not opened and is a museum item, so it is not cited.
Whether the 2000 master plan was completed is not verified.

sites.name: CHARLOTTE ARMY MIS PL

facts.summary: WFAE reported in July 2017 that ATCO bought the roughly 75-acre site in December 2016 for about $17 million. The new owners planned to keep the historic plant buildings and make the site resemble its 1920s look. The rezoning from general industrial to mixed-use was still pending then.
facts.reference: Former Model T missile factory: redevelopment part of Camp North End
facts.quote: ATCO, which bought the 75-acre site last December for about $17 million.

facts.summary: Charlotte City Council approved a rezoning for the 72-acre Camp North End development in September 2017. The county landmark record names this site the Charlotte Area Missile Plant at 300 Camp Road. At the time, ATCO's plans called for up to 1,500 apartments and 1.5 million square feet of office space.
facts.reference: Council approves 72-acre Camp North End rezoning
facts.quote: The Charlotte City Council on Monday approved a rezoning for the 72-acre Camp North End development

facts.summary: WSOC reported in May 2023 that work was underway on Atco Properties' first apartment community at Camp North End, Kinship. It is a two-building, 240,390-square-foot project with 301 units and an estimated completion in early 2025. The article quotes plans to eventually develop up to 1,800 total units on the site. Completion was not verified.
facts.reference: Work first apartments coming to Camp North End begins
facts.quote: Work is underway on Atco Properties’ first apartment community at Camp North End.

facts.summary: Atlanta-based Jamestown joined the ownership of the 76-acre Camp North End as general partner and lead asset manager. ATCO remains a partner, and Shorenstein remains a partner in a portion of the project. The investment amount was not disclosed. PointBlank Ventures was retained to raise joint-venture equity for the next phases.
facts.reference: Jamestown Joins Ownership Group at 76-Acre Camp North End Campus in Charlotte
facts.quote: Jamestown has partnered with existing ownership to recapitalize Camp North End

facts.summary: WFAE reported in February 2026 that the property is entitled for up to 3.2 million square feet of additional development. The new owners said they want more housing, retail, and food and beverage tenants. The article gives no phase plan or unit count.
facts.reference: Changes in ownership at Camp North End
facts.quote: The property is entitled for up to 3.2 million square feet of additional development.

gaps: Matched to this site because the Mecklenburg County landmark record identifies the Charlotte Quartermaster Depot / Charlotte Area Missile Plant at 300 Camp Road as 'the Camp Road property now comprising Camp North End'. News coverage uses the Hercules Industrial Park and Camp North End names.
The Axios February 2026 article on Jamestown returned HTTP 403 and was not opened. Nothing from it is cited.
No dated, opened source was found for the phase-two plans beyond the 2026 entitlement figure. The WSOC next-phase headline was not opened in full.
Kinship's completion date is not verified from an opened page.
Acreage differs by source (72 acres in the rezoning story, 75 to 76 acres for the site). Not resolved.
No community benefit, incentive, or cleanup item was found in news for this site.
